learning_objective: 🎯 Master the timeline of English! Learn the rules of the 12 tenses to accurately express when an action happens (Past, Present, or Future) without grammatical errors.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Used for habits, facts, or finished actions. Present Simple: Subject + V1(s/es) (e.g., 'He plays'). Past Simple: Subject + V2 (e.g., 'He played' - the ONLY tense where V2 is used!). Future Simple: Subject + will/shall + V1 (e.g., 'He will play').

Used for actions happening right now or at a specific moment. Rule: 'Be' verb + V1-ing. Present: is/am/are + V-ing. Past: was/were + V-ing. Future: will be + V-ing. (e.g., 'I am playing', 'I was playing').

Used for actions that are already completed before another action or time. Rule: 'Have' verb + V3 (Past Participle). Present: has/have + V3. Past: had + V3. Future: will have + V3. (e.g., 'I have eaten', 'I had eaten').

Used for actions that started in the past and are STILL continuing. Rule: has/have/had + been + V1-ing + since/for. Use 'since' for a fixed point of time (Since Monday, Since 2015) and 'for' for a duration (For 2 hours, For 5 years).

fun_activity.title: 🕵️ The Time Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Look out for 'clue words' in sentences! 'Every day', 'Usually', 'Often' = Present Simple. 'Yesterday', 'Last night', 'In 2010' = Past Simple. 'Tomorrow', 'Next week' = Future Simple. Find 3 sentences in your textbook and become a Time Detective by identifying their tenses!

exam_tips: 📌 Universal truths and scientific facts are ALWAYS written in Simple Present Tense (e.g., 'The earth revolves around the sun' - not 'revolved' or 'is revolving').
📌 'Did' always takes V1 (Base form of the verb). Never use 'Did' with V2! (Correct: 'Did he go?' | Incorrect: 'Did he went?').
📌 If a sentence has two past actions, the one that happened FIRST takes Past Perfect (had + V3), and the SECOND takes Past Simple (V2). e.g., 'The train had left before I reached the station.'
quick_recap: ⭐ V3 (Past Participle) is NEVER used alone without a helping verb (has/have/had).
⭐ 'Since' is for exact starting time (Point of time); 'For' is for total duration (Period of time).
⭐ Stative verbs (like, love, hate, know, believe) are generally NOT used in continuous (-ing) forms.
